title: Unary internal Hom derives to internal RHom from a degree-zero module
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $M$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module, and $T_M=\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(M,-)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom], assumed additive. Let $S:D(\mathcal O_X)\to D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category] with comparison $\delta:T_M^{\bullet}Q\to QS$ be a right derived functor of termwise internal Hom, for quasi-isomorphisms. Then $S$ is naturally isomorphic to $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(M[0],-)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. No local freeness, algebra structure, or adjunction is assumed.

proof.text: Choose the functorial K-injective resolution in O_X-modules. The K-injective right derivability structure computes any right derived functor S of termwise Hom on those representatives, with its comparison invertible there. Termwise additive Hom preserves homotopy equivalences, and quasi-isomorphisms between K-injectives are homotopy equivalences; hence the K-injective localizer derives termwise Hom followed by Q.

The existing homComplex_single_iso identifies Hom-complex(M[0],I) with degreewise Hom(M,I). Its projection onto the sole surviving factor is natural in I by the map formula of homComplex_exists; insert zero in the other factors for its inverse. This upgrades the objectwise comparison to a natural chain isomorphism.

Specialize derivedInternalHom_comparison to M[0] and the same K-injective resolution. Compose with the preceding natural chain isomorphism. Descend along the K-injective localization equivalence, or use uniqueness of the right derived functor, to obtain S isomorphic to RHom(M[0],-). No exactness or local freeness of M is assumed; the argument includes zero M and unbounded target complexes.
